root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `json_tokener_parse_ex()` resolves a pending high surrogate or enters the EOF cleanup path that reuses one, the current `\uNNNN` escape must already have consumed all four hex digits (`tok->st_pos == 4`). If fewer than four digits are available, the parser must return with the partial escape state intact instead of reusing stale-surrogate logic.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the later pending-surrogate resolution gate after the second escape has consumed only one hex digit (`tok->st_pos == 1`), so the missing completion check is violated while the stale high-surrogate cleanup still executes. The fixed original stops before that gate on the staged witness, and the adjacent `complete_second_escape_zero_fill` perturbation executes the same protected gate with `tok->st_pos == 4`, giving a genuine witness for the required obligation.

nodes.state: The vulnerable EOF cleanup compares `tok->pb->buf` against the 3-byte global `utf8_replacement_char` with `strcmp`, producing the AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow read when that compare executes.

The first decoded escape stores the attacker-derived high surrogate in `tok->got_hi_surrogate`; that stale surrogate value is later reused when the second escape reaches the pending-surrogate resolution gate.

When the first high surrogate is not immediately followed by another `\u`, the parser appends `utf8_replacement_char` into `tok->pb`; that same print-buffer object later becomes the left argument of the crashing cleanup `strcmp`.

edges.relation: The same incomplete digit count captured after the lone `d` in the second escape (`tok->st_pos == 1`) reaches the later pending-surrogate resolution gate unchanged, proving the vulnerable cleanup runs with an unfinished `\uNNNN` sequence.
Once the vulnerable code reaches the pending-surrogate resolution gate with stale `tok->got_hi_surrogate`, that same stale surrogate state immediately gates the cleanup `strcmp` sink.
The pending high surrogate saved from the first escape remains unchanged in `tok->got_hi_surrogate` when the later second escape reaches the vulnerable pending-surrogate resolution gate.
The print-buffer object that received `utf8_replacement_char` after the first lone high surrogate is the same `tok->pb->buf` object later passed into the crashing cleanup `strcmp`.
